lede: The story of Christmas in Anna starts with the Houston and Texas Central Railway, which passed through in 1873, and the town platted in 1883, and today it centers on the city's 12 Days of Anna, with free ice skating on Anna Municipal Plaza. Anna has 2 events on this page, led by Free Ice Skating on Friday, December 4, 2026.
sections: John F. Greer arrived in 1867 and is credited with building the first home and store in what became Anna, even though Collin McKinney had settled a few miles away in 1846. The Houston and Texas Central Railway, then building between Dallas and Denison, passed through in 1873. When Anna was platted in 1883 it had twenty people, two stores, a steam gristmill and a Baptist church, and a post office opened that year. By 1890 the town had 100 to 200 residents, and it incorporated in 1913 with Greer as its first mayor. The Continental Bank, Anna's first, was organized in 1902.

The Handbook of Texas records four explanations for the name Anna. Some sources say it honors Greer's daughter. Others say it honors Anna Quinlan, daughter of George A. Quinlan, a former superintendent of the Houston and Texas Central. A third story makes Anna Quinlan the wife of Quinlan and the daughter of J. L. Greer, and a fourth credits Anna Huntington, daughter of C. P. Huntington, who built the Dallas to Denison line. The town stayed small for a long time: 904 people in 1990 and 1,225 in 2000. The Texas Almanac lists 16,896 for 2020 and 20,243 for 2021.

The City of Anna runs 12 Days of Anna as a community holiday celebration. For 2026, Day 1 on Friday, December 4 puts an ice rink on Anna Municipal Plaza with a free Adaptive Skate, Open Skate and a Teen Glow Skate, and Day 3 on Sunday, December 6 is free skating from 9 am to 9 pm, with hot chocolate from the Anna Band Boosters from 2 to 3:30 pm. The Anna Community Library hosts Letters to Santa and Movie Night on December 10 and Graham Cracker House Construction on December 11. The city's page also lists Santa's Village activities on December 5.
trains: Anna grew up on the Houston and Texas Central Railway in 1873, and in 1915 the Greenville and Whitewright Northern Traction Company built the Greenville and Northwestern Railway between Anna and Blue Ridge, a line that was abandoned in 1920. DART's Red Line runs from Parker Road Station in Plano to Westmoreland Station in Dallas. For a train outing, the Interurban Railway Museum is in Plano, the Museum of the American Railroad is in Frisco and the McKinney Avenue M-Line Trolley runs in Dallas.

kidfact: Anna has four different stories about how it got its name, and the Handbook of Texas does not pick a winner.
faq: How did Anna get its name?

The Handbook of Texas lists four stories. One says the town honors a daughter of John F. Greer. Others name Anna Quinlan, tied to Houston and Texas Central official George A. Quinlan, or Anna Huntington, daughter of railroad builder C. P. Huntington. No single story is confirmed, so the town's name remains a small local mystery.

The Houston and Texas Central Railway passed through the area in 1873, and Anna was platted in 1883 with twenty residents, two stores, a steam gristmill and a Baptist church. A post office opened that year. The town incorporated in 1913 with John F. Greer as its first mayor, according to the Handbook of Texas.
What was the Greenville and Northwestern Railway?

In 1915 the Greenville and Whitewright Northern Traction Company built the Greenville and Northwestern Railway between Anna and Blue Ridge by way of Westminster. The Handbook of Texas says the line proved unsuccessful and was abandoned in 1920, so Anna's main rail link remained the Houston and Texas Central line.
What is the 12 Days of Anna?

The City of Anna describes 12 Days of Anna as a community holiday celebration. In 2026 it includes free ice skating on Anna Municipal Plaza on December 4 and 6, Santa's Village activities on December 5, a Letters to Santa movie night on December 10 and graham cracker houses at the library on December 11.

Anna was small for most of its history, with 904 people in 1990 and 1,225 in 2000. The Texas Almanac lists 8,249 for 2010, 16,896 for 2020 and 20,243 for 2021. The 2020 census count was under 20,000, and the 2021 figure shows how quickly the town has been growing.
